citations.quote: The main objective is to guide teams with a software which provides a clear design solution for the introduced mission requirement using COTS products with flight heritage. GREATCUBE+ is capable of performing this task via an intensive usage of empirical correlations, derived from a database of successfully flown missions, analytical equations directly retrieved from literature, and numerical analysis.

Its layered structure comprises three levels: empirical, where successfully flown missions are used for an initial tradeoff; analytical, where a design refinement is performed; and numerical, for the final assessment of the proposed architecture.

GREATCUBE+ provides, at the end of its operations, a complete design of the CubeSat in terms of weights, volumes, and power requirement. Additionally, it is comprehensive of a detailed list of COTS which are up to the task of satisfying the current mission requirements and a final CubeSat model in an initial graphics exchange specification (IGES) format with the previously mentioned COTS as subsystems.

Phase 0 and phase A are the ideal scenarios for the implementation of GREATCUBE+ because they are the sections in which the conceptual development takes place. Teams could use this tool while discussing the mission requirements in order to already have a model to perform an initial analysis on.

GC+ is a plug-and-play type of software. To perform simulations with it, the user must have a valid MATLAB license, FreeCAD, and Python. If this software are available, the user can run the Run Me.m file and press run to start a simulation. No in-depth analysis of the code is necessary in order to operate the tool. To successfully operate GREATCUBE+. it is only necessary to answer the series of questions which are posed throughout the simulation.

GREATCUBE+ Empirical Level (GEL) is the initial layer of GREATCUBE+ which uses empirical correlations to build up a COTS based model. The empirical correlations are retrieved from a database of flown missions. GEL links user-introduced inputs with system and subsystem values.

GREATCUBE+ Analytical Level (GAL) is the second layer of GREATCUBE+. It uses well-proven analytical equations to perform a refinement of the COTS-based model inherited from GEL. As output, it produces a new COTS-based model, which is expected to have an increased quality when comparing it to the one proposed in GEL.

GREATCUBE+ Numerical Level (GNL) is the final layer of GREATCUBE+. The analytical model inherited by GAL does not provide any information on the position of the COTS products recommended. GNL uses a genetic algorithm with three optimizing functions to assess the position of the subsystems. The goals are to respect the center-of-gravity (COG) requirement of the launcher and specific positions for certain subsystems.
